absent: Early portion of device operations table before virtual function section was not routed so lifecycle transmit receive and basic configuration callbacks remain unknown.
Calling context locking and error semantics for database bridge slave feature and offload hooks are not shown.
Allocation registration teardown and notification flows that drive registration state changes are not shown.
Layout and meaning of referenced auxiliary structures for queues statistics filters programs and hardware state are not shown.
Concrete flag combinations queue sizing rules and address list management beyond lock presence are not shown.

findings.text: The tail of the device operations table collects driver callbacks by functional area, covering virtual function identity, traffic control, storage offload, slave selection, feature negotiation, neighbour handling, forwarding databases, bridging, link and port identity, queue control, metadata, packet framework integration, tunneling, peer lookup, path resolution and time stamping, with optional shaping operations when enabled.

Drivers can provide hooks to query and assign virtual function identity and spreading preferences, to apply traffic control settings via ndo_setup_tc with type tag and opaque data, to enable Fibre Channel sessions with direct placement by exchange identifier, and to steer receive flows for acceleration.

Stacking and forwarding hooks support adding and removing slaves, selecting transmit slaves and lower devices, normalizing then applying features, handling neighbours, and maintaining forwarding and multicast databases via ndo_fdb_add and ndo_mdb_add style operations keyed by address and tag with notification feedback, alongside bridge link handling.

Link path and offload hooks cover carrier changes via ndo_change_carrier, port identity and naming, forward attach with private context, queue rates, metadata and headroom, packet commands via ndo_bpf, high speed transmit and wakeup, tunneling and peer lookup, path fill, and stamp configuration via ndo_hwtstamp_set.
When Fibre Channel library support is present the world wide name selector uses zero for node identity and one for port identity.

Private flags use distinct single bit positions with shifts zero through twenty two and twenty four through twenty nine, plus wide helper forms for thirty and thirty one, leaving shift twenty three unassigned.

Private flags record internal roles such as virtual LAN bridging bonding teaming and overlay membership, address and queue behavior, offload participation, master slave layering, and suppression of generic handling including bridging polling address configuration and receive dispatch.

Registration progresses from uninitialized to registered after completion, to unregistering when removal starts, to unregistered after deferred work finishes, to released after deallocation, with a separate dummy value for polling contexts that never register.

Small discriminators select mid layer private ownership with none default and controller area variant, select which per CPU statistics layout is active among none and three options, and select transmit memory mode among unsupported direct capable and virtual pass through without direct access.

The descriptor separates hot path state into transmit combined and receive cacheline groups, with transmit keeping operation tables and queue state plus size fields such as mtu, combined keeping statistics and feature sets, and receive keeping program state such as xdp_prog with index fields such as ifindex.

Control state carries naming alias and hardware address identity via name, perm_addr and dev_addr, device queue adjacency and upper lower lists, hardware requested virtual and encapsulation feature sets, size bounds type and group, legacy plus per CPU statistics with link flap counters, subsystem operation tables, and configuration queue shaper and offload state.

Queueing and lifetime state includes queue counts arrays discipline hash and locks, bulk queues, watchdog timer, deferred work lists, reference counts with tracking, notifier lists, page pools, moderation and pacing controls, registration state in reg_state, mutual exclusion in lock, and trailing private storage sized by priv_len in priv with alignment.

A per device mutex in lock is taken after the global link configuration lock, with virtual before physical when both are needed for queue leasing. It guards timeouts deferrals polling lists shaper hierarchy registration and threading, shares up flag namespace move network pointer and extended features with either lock enough for readers, and extends to configuration queue counts and callback state for drivers opting into expanded coverage via request_ops_lock.

Size field mtu is often read without holding a lock while writers use link configuration protection, with single access helpers advised. Address transmit and watchdog state have dedicated spin locks. Many filter program table and protocol pointers use read copy update, and a cached up flag may report false negatives during open or close because that path is not covered.

Segmentation ceilings are fixed with legacy receive offload at 65536 and large form at 8 times 65535, segmentation segments at 65535 with legacy size 65536 and large size 8 times the segment limit, and transmit segmentation legacy at 65536 with maximum size at unsigned maximum and segment count at sixteen bit maximum.
Device alignment requirement is 32 bytes.
A helper derives the enclosing network device descriptor from its embedded generic device member.
Binding a devlink port in devlink_port is valid only while registration in reg_state remains uninitialized, with misuse producing a warning while still recording the supplied port.
Generic receive offload is skipped when the offload feature is absent or when program state in xdp_prog is attached.

Priority to class mapping in prio_tc_map is accessed with masking on priority and class, writes are rejected when the class meets or exceeds the active count in num_tc, and the active count is exposed through a dedicated accessor.
Network prefetch helpers prepare packet memory for read or write access, issuing an extra line fetch when the first level cache line is narrow, building on a write intent primitive.

Lockless size reads risk stale or torn views without single access discipline, late devlink binding signals ordering misuse, and incorrect role flags may divert bridging polling addressing or receive handling.
Size priority and count reads rely on an external single access primitive owned elsewhere.
Priority mapping updates rely on an external single access store primitive owned elsewhere.
